Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training.
Experience designing and implementing wireless networks.
Experience in a university or research environment.

Knowledge of network equipment such as routers, switches, firewalls, wireless access points, VoIP, IP address management and supporting equipment and software. Experience troubleshooting network, telephone and cable problems in multi-building campus-type environments.

Extensive working knowledge of industry standard cabling distribution/termination skills, techniques and methods, and experience working in cable communication/network equipment closets. Applied knowledge of category 6A cabling standards and the skills and ability to independently apply the standards to cable installation, termination and repair.
3-5 yearsof experience in telecommunications.

Under the general supervision of the Manager, Telecom Engineers and Field Technicians, the Network and Telecommunications Technician is responsible for the installation, maintenance and repair of campus telephone and network infrastructure and services. This includes supporting the campus’ Mitel PBX telephone system alongside the ongoing migration to Microsoft Teams Phone, UCI’s cloud-based voice platform, through installations, upgrades, moves/adds/changes and repairs. Plans and implements projects related to telecommunications and network infrastructure, including wireless network design and cabling. Maintains accurate records and documentation. Performs all work with professionalism and a focus on customer service.
Adhere to OIT’s cultural values: Collaboration, Respect, Trust, Transparency, Quality, Inclusiveness, Customer Centricity, and Learning and Growth.
May be required to work overtime.
May be required to be on an on-call rotation.
Skills, knowledge and ability to independently install, maintain, and troubleshoot a variety of voice and network communications equipment and related cable systems.
Working knowledge of cloud-based voice platforms such as Microsoft Teams Phone.

Working knowledge of network systems and technologies - including but not limited to communications cabling systems, Ethernet LANs, network switches, routers, TCP/IP protocol, Ethernet network backbones, and other fiber-optic based networks.
Ability to understand the communications and network service needs of campus organizations and to acquire and apply skills needed to implement, maintain and document solutions.
Ability to independently interpret technical documents and schematics associated with voice and network systems, topologies, equipment and configurations.
Ability to independently create and/or follow a detailed installation plan.

Skilled in the use of electronic test equipment (i.e., twisted pair cable tester, tone set, butt-set, fiber optic test equipment, VOM/multimeter, etc.) and PC-based trouble shooting software. Skilled in the use of the tools of the trade (i.e., punch tools, wire wrap tool cutters, strippers, crimpers, and other manual and power hand tools).
Working knowledge of principles of operation and capabilities of network hardware and software to solve a broad range of common network related problems that arise with the production environment.
Ability to learn specialty programs used by the OIT network and voice engineering team to manage and solve trouble as it occurs.
Proficient with computer applications for calendaring, spreadsheets, and documentation such as the Microsoft Office suite.
Strong communication and interpersonal skills, and ability to work independently and as a team member.
Basic understanding and ability to use on-line work order systems and time keeping systems.
Ability to comply with all safety procedures and regulations in accordance with UC Irvine Environmental Health and Safety and other industry recognized safety organizations.
Extensive working knowledge of standards based cable color codes and cable termination methods on punch blocks and other termination equipment.
Working knowledge of both Macintosh and Windows operating systems.
